problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

feedback.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j \\  & =i+2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}(\,i+2t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$
